1 big thing: A Nobel for neutrinos
 
Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios

Belgian-born scientist Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in physics today for his efforts to demystify a rare group of neutrinos — tiny cosmic particles that could hint at how the universe evolved.

  • Halzen told the Nobel Physics Committee: "It was a great surprise, and I obviously didn't expect it."

🔎 Neutrinos have no electric charge and extraordinarily small mass, making them hard to detect.

  • Yet they are everywhere. They spew from stars like the sun, and trillions zip through our bodies every second.

👩‍🔬 Scientists can't glimpse them zooming around on their own, so they measure what happens when they collide with other bits of matter.

  • But neutrinos bump into other particles only rarely, so researchers build large detectors to improve their odds of catching collisions.

🧊 Halzen had the idea to turn the vast Antarctic ice into such a detector.

  • The Nobel committee said his work was instrumental to the construction of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory in Antarctica, which glimpsed the first high-energy neutrinos from faraway galaxies.

2. 🤖 AI boom drives record imports
 
Data: U.S. Census Bureau; Chart: Courtenay Brown/Axios

U.S. imports hit a record $421 billion in August, Axios' Courtenay Brown reports from new government data.

  • Imports rose much faster than exports, widening the U.S. trade deficit by about 14% to $106 billion. (Still, the trade gap is about 20% smaller this year than at the same time last year.)

💻 Imports of semiconductors — critical to the data centers and computing infrastructure behind the AI buildout — jumped by a record $2.4 billion from July.

  • Crude oil imports also rose sharply.

The numbers underscore a tension at the heart of Trump's economic agenda: The administration wants to curb imports while accelerating an AI boom that heavily depends on them.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
President Trump at a rally last night in Grand Island, Neb. Photo: Win McNamee/Getty Images
  1. 😡 California leaders are blasting President Trump after he said during a rally last night, about Iran: "Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego." The White House claims that Trump was talking about stopping Iran from attacking those cities. Get the latest.
  2. 👩‍💼 Sally Yates, a deputy attorney general in the Obama administration, will oversee a review into Cornell University's handling of sexual misconduct complaints. That comes amid widespread anger over how the school dealt with allegations of a 2024 gang rape at a fraternity house. Get the latest.
  3. 🍿 Paramount Skydance closed its deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, ending a dramatic, yearlong process that rattled Hollywood, Wall Street and Washington. The deal creates one of the world's largest entertainment behemoths and makes CEO David Ellison one of the most powerful people in culture and business. More from Sara Fischer.
 
 
4. ✈️ 1 for the road: Aspen flight fight
 
Illustration: Shoshana Gordon/Axios

Planned upgrades to Aspen's airport sit at the core of a broader fight over the future of the iconic Colorado ski town, Andrew Zucker reports in The Wall Street Journal.

  • The plan calls for shifting the roughly 8,000-foot runway 80 feet to the west and widening it to 150 feet, to accommodate bigger jets used by some of the ultra-wealthy visitors who've become a staple of the Aspen crowd.

🛬 Proponents say that mountainous, hard-to-reach Aspen will benefit from easier access by air.

  • Detractors worry about being overrun with visitors — and the economic shock from closing the airfield for several months to do the work.
